Protect Your Business Against Product-Related Claims

A Product Liability Insurance Policy protects manufacturers, importers, distributors and sellers against legal liability arising from third-party bodily injury or property damage caused by defective products.

What Does Product Liability Insurance Cover?
A Product Liability Insurance Policy covers legal liability arising out of Third-Party Bodily Injury or Property Damage caused by using an Insured Company’s Defective products. The Defects covered by a Product Liability Insurance Policy include:
1. Manufacturing Defects
2. Design Defects
3. Failure to Warn or Labeling defects
The Policy pays for legal fees, settlements and court-awarded damages arising out of such claims

What is an Erection All Risk (EAR) Insurance Policy?
An Erection All Risk (EAR) Insurance Policy offers comprehensive coverage for machinery erection, installation, testing, and commissioning against unforeseen losses, along with third-party liability protection at the project site.

What does an EAR Policy Cover?
An EAR Policy covers:
• Physical loss or damage during erection, installation, testing & commissioning
• Fire, explosion, collapse, and accidental damage
• Losses due to handling errors, negligence, or human error
• Losses due to Natural calamities such as storm, flood, and earthquake if opted
• Third-party bodily injury and property damage
• Optional covers like debris removal and extended maintenance

An EAR Policy minimises financial impact of accidents at project sites. 

Who needs to purchase an EAR Insurance Policy?
An EAR Insurance Policy is ideal for:
• EPC Contractors 
• Power & Industrial Projects 
• Heavy Engineering 
• Infrastructure Projects

What is a Commercial General Liability (CGL) Insurance Policy?
A Commercial General Liability (CGL) Insurance Policy protects a company against legal liability from third-party claims of bodily injury, property damage, personal or advertising injury or medical payments related to a business's premises, operations, products, or completed work.

What Does CGL Insurance Cover?
• Third-party bodily injury or property damage claims arising from business operations, products, or premises
• Legal Claims arising from defamation, libel, slander, copyright infringement in ads, and violation of personal rights
• Medical Payments

Who needs to buy a CGL Insurance Policy?
CGL is essential public facing businesses such as :
• Schools
• Malls

featured_reviews.name: Karan Beri
featured_reviews.review_text:
The New India Assurance Building is a striking architectural gem located at 87, Mahatma Gandhi Road in the historic Fort district of Mumbai, India. Completed in 1937 and designed by the firm Master, Sathe and Bhuta, with artistic input from N. G. Pansare, this six-story office structure stands as a prime example of Art Deco architecture with an Indian twist — often described as Indo-Deco.  
Wikipedia +1
What immediately captivates visitors is its bold façade, characterized by pronounced vertical ribs that create a sense of grandeur and height, despite the building’s moderate scale. At street level, detailed bas-relief sculptures depict scenes of everyday life — Indian farmers, industrial workers, and traditional attire — seamlessly blending local culture with the streamlined geometric forms of Art Deco. These artistic reliefs don’t just decorate the building; they narrate India’s social and economic spirit during the pre-independence era.  
Wikipedia +1
The design also reflects an early appreciation for climate-responsive architecture. Projections on the east and west façades help shield windows from direct sunlight, and operable windows allow airflow — thoughtful features for Mumbai’s tropical environment long before modern HVAC systems were commonplace.  
Around Us
Design aficionados and heritage lovers regard the New India Assurance Building as a key component of the Victorian Gothic and Art Deco Ensemble of Mumbai, a UNESCO World Heritage site. Its aesthetic appeal lies not just in ornamentation but in how it communicates confidence, modernity and Indian identity at a time when corporate architecture was often dominated by colonial European styles.  
Wikipedia
Inside, the building continues to function as an office — it serves as a headquarters for the New India Assurance Company Ltd, a long-established insurance provider founded in 1919 by Sir Dorabji Tata that has grown into one of India’s biggest general insurers.  
New India
In summary, the New India Assurance Building is far more than an ordinary office block. It’s a cultural and architectural landmark that captures a unique historical moment — where global design trends met indigenous expression — and continues to be appreciated by historians, architects, and everyday passersby in Mumbai’s bustling Fort area.
